newsitem.title: UK: Jaguar confirms it looking at small car.
newsitem.headline: Jaguar confirms it looking at small car.

text.p: Britain's Jaguar Cars Ltd on Tuesday confirmed it had launched a study into a new, smaller car which would double its annual output.
It is unlikely that the car -- called the X400 -- would ever be built in Britain, however.
The company, owned by Ford Motor Co of the U.S., said it had been "actively looking" at the market for cars of the size of the highly successful BMW 3-Series.
"It is a viable market for Jaguar and we have started a feasibility study," spokesman Colin Cook told Reuters in response to press reports. The study will take about three months.

He said the car, if it went into production, would hit the market early next century. Press reports of a development cost of $600 million were not Jaguar's figures, he said. He would not give a figure.
The car would be a saloon designed to compete head-on with the BMW 3-Series, the Mercedes C-Class and the Audi A4.
"We would be competing with the market's premium brands," Cook said.
The new car would probably be built in volumes of around 100,000 a year. Jaguar builds less than 50,000 cars a year. Its range consists of the large XJ saloons and XK8 sports car.

But it already plans to launch a new, mid-sized car -- the X200 -- in 1999 which will take its annual output to around 100,000. That car will be the smallest Jaguar ever built, but the X400 would be smaller.
Cook said that Jaguar's two British plants -- in Coventry and Castle Bromwich in central England -- already had capacity problems so the X400 would probably have to be built at a foreign plant.
"It would be very difficult to expand our existing plants and we would not build a new plant in Britain," he said.
After years of heavy losses, Jaguar is now profitable and has made considerable productivity improvements in recent years.
Ford bought Jaguar for $2.5 billion in 1989. --Ashley Seager, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
